text:
alex: Quick weekly headroom check — I pulled run-hours and queue depth for the next 7 days. Posting raw numbers, need quick triage and hedges.

alex: TL;DR: US cluster headroom down to ~6% by Thu if current burst continues. EU has ~14% buffer, APAC is healthy but network egress to US is flakey.

alex: Raw: 
```
Projection window: next 7 days
US-west-prod: projected GPU hours 18,700 (capacity 19,900) => headroom ~6%
eu-west-cluster-a: projected 11,800 / capacity 13,700 => headroom ~14%
apac-north-cluster: projected 4,200 / capacity 6,500 => headroom ~35%
Spot/Preemptible utilization: US 62%, EU 28%, APAC 18%
Average seq len (prod gen): US 520, EU 480, APAC 300
Queue p95 wait (US): 1.9s and trending up
```

sre-bot: Alert: US-west-prod headroom <10% threshold. Auto-scaler will not preempt SLO-critical routes.

maria: Noted. What's driving the US burst — fine-tuned model rollout? marketing campaign?

alex: It's two things: 1) new internal A/B on default model size (more tokens), 2) a weekend campaign from partner that spikes short-latency calls (lots of small requests adding queue overhead).

devon: Can we push batchable requests to a cheaper queue? We can throttle non-SLO routes by 20% and move them to eu-west until Thu morning.

ashley: We already have a partial policy for non-critical embedding jobs to go to preemptible. Are these jobs labeled correctly? I see some partner jobs still tagged as prod.

alex: Correct, partner jobs are marked prod because same API route. We discussed route-splitting last week. Ask: can we create a temporary route alias to route partner traffic to a dedicated preemptible-backed pool?

maria: Ops-wise, yes. But there's a 45m lead time for infra changes and we should notify partner. Is it acceptable to route them to preemptible? Latency SLO will be softer.

kai: Network note: APAC->US egress packet loss spiked overnight (0.6% -> 1.8%) which causes some retries and increases token load in US. If partner calls originate in APAC, that explains part of the US pressure. We're running a traceroute with the provider now.

alex: Proposed short hedges: 
- Create partner-temp-route -> preemptible US pool (owner: devon, ETA: 45m)
- Throttle partner route to 60% of current QPS at edge (owner: maria, ETA: 15m)
- Move low-priority batch jobs to eu-west for 24h (owner: ashley, ETA: 30m)
- Enable ephemeral burst-capacity request for US (reserve +120 T4s, cost estimate ~$3.6k/day) if headroom still <8% after above (owner: infra-oncall, ETA: requires approval)

devon: I can create the route and wire it to preemptible pool. Will add a header check so internal traffic uses prod path.

maria: I'll apply edge throttle and add partner notification template.

ashley: I'll scan batch job labels and kick the move for jobs with tag batch=low. Expect ~18% reduction in US load.

alex: If we still need burst-reserve, I'll loop in finance for fast approval. Ping me in #finance if we need override.

sre-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance in eu-west tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC — some reduced capacity expected. That reduces effective EU headroom by ~3%.

kai: Given maintenance, let's only shift strictly non-SLO workloads to eu-west. Re-calculating numbers shortly.

alex: Follow-ups: devon will create route (2951234600), maria will throttle (2951234610), ashley will move batch jobs (2951234595). We'll reconvene in thread in 1h. Thanks. :thumbsup:
